summary: Feed s128_double is degraded: 100% of packets missing required VLANs 10/20 (tags stripped) and 27.22 Gbps microbursts overload the 10 Gbps APM port (272% capacity), causing segmentation blindness and burst packet loss.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or upstream SPAN/TAP is stripping 802.1Q tags before delivery. 100% of packets arrived untagged despite APM requiring VLANs 10 and 20, typical when broker egress is set to strip tags or SPAN is configured as access port.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM cannot segment traffic by VLAN 10/20 for application/tenant isolation; per-VLAN latency, error rates and transaction traces are misclassified or invisible, reducing detection coverage for VLAN-specific performance issues.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to preserve and forward 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10 and 20 to the APM so it can correctly classify and monitor segmented traffic.

findings.root_cause: Single 10 Gbps APM port fed without load balancing; 1 ms microburst peaked at 27.22 Gbps (272% of capacity, >80% threshold), exceeding port line rate and broker egress buffers.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM ingress drops packets during bursts, causing incomplete transaction traces, skewed latency/error metrics, and missed APM alerts due to random loss under overload.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across multiple APM ports/tool group via packet broker flow-hash load balancing to keep per-port utilization below 80% and absorb microbursts without drops.
